subject: Forecasted usage surge, target $/1M tokens and approval ladder
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@vertexai.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@vertexai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Forecasted usage surge, target $/1M tokens and approval ladder

Hi Liam / Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the specific asks you outlined on procurement and pricing: 

- Expected steady-state monthly token consumption: 50M–80M for initial rollout.
- Potential surge window (Q3 pilot → Q4 GA) estimating 120M–180M/mo if the embedding-heavy search and personalization workloads scale as expected.
- Target unit economics for finance: $70–$110 per 1M tokens (goal is to land closer to $80 if we can secure a short-term commit).
- Procurement constraints: Finance requires a formal PO for any monthly spend > $25k and prefers 3–6 month commitments for vendor onboarding.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
1) I will share a pricing stencil (attached) illustrating three commitment scenarios (no commit, 3mo commit, 12mo commit) and the corresponding $/1M token tiers.
2) You share a rough monthly spend band you can approve for a pilot (range is fine). Procurement also asked for a single-line estimate they can use for internal PO thresholds.
3) If the band lands above $25k/mo, we will loop in your procurement contact to accelerate PO.

Also attaching a lightweight Mutual Action Plan so we can agree timelines (attachment: vertexai_map_v1.docx).

If it helps, my recommendation to keep momentum is: offer a 3‑month pilot commit (minimum) at a mid-tier discount — that typically unlocks a better $/1M and keeps legal/PO friction low. Jordan and Karthik — would appreciate your quick nod on offering a two‑tier pilot discount (3mo / 12mo) for this type of account.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: redwood_pricing_stencil_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), vertexai_map_v1.docx (MAP)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@vertexai.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@vertexai.com>, procure@vertexai.com
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Forecasted usage surge, target $/1M tokens and approval ladder

Thanks Aisha — solid recap. A few clarifications from our end: 

- The 50M–80M/mo is realistic for our initial pilot; we can budget for a short burst to ~130M/mo for a 4–6 week test during product launch.
- Finance wants a single-line estimate for the PO packet. At the moment they will approve up to $20k/mo without a formal PO; above that they need PO and a vendor onboarding form.
- Target $/1M: our CFO prefers seeing pricing under $100/1M for committed terms; $80/1M would be ideal but may require a guaranteed minimum.

I'll review the attachments and capture a single-line estimate this afternoon. Looping in procurement so they can flag any vendor requirements early.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product, VertexAI Solutions
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Forecasted usage surge, target $/1M tokens and approval ladder — pricing ask

Jordan / Karthik — forwarding Liam's note and procurement constraint. Key ask: can we authorize offering a 3‑month pilot at $85/1M for committed volume >= 60M/mo (monthly true‑up), and a fallback PAYG tier at $125/1M for non‑committed usage?

Why this structure: it gets VertexAI under contract quickly (PO) for the pilot window while protecting our unit economics during burst usage. If they convert to a 12mo commit, we can tier down to $70/1M.

If you approve, I'll: 
- Finalize the pricing stencil with those bands.
- Prepare a short commercial summary for procurement (single-line estimate for PO).
- Offer an implementation quickstart (free credits for the first 2 weeks) to reduce time to value.

We should also decide if we need legal to do a quick review or if standard T&Cs suffice for a sub-$100k pilot.

Thanks —
Aisha
